headline: Cisco's 9.8 auth bypass leads a three-CVE exploited docket
standfirst: All three CVEs in today's selection are KEV-listed and reported as exploited: a Critical Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager authentication bypass, a High-severity Zimbra command injection hit before disclosure, and an Apple CoreGraphics memory-corruption bug that now has a public proof-of-concept. Below them sit breach confirmations from the Pentagon, Bitget and DIVD, a ransomware takedown with an alleged teenage administrator, and fresh numbers on GitHub secret sprawl.
bodyMarkdown:
## Actively exploited

CISA added CVE-2026-76504 to KEV after reports of active exploitation, and it is the day's most urgent item [[s30]]. NVD rates it 9.8 Critical and describes improper URI-encoding handling in an HTTP request that defeats an authentication rule guarding a specific API endpoint; a crafted request reaches that API with admin privileges, over the network, with no credentials and no user interaction. Affected Catalyst SD-WAN Manager ranges are those below 20.9.10.1, below 20.12.8.2, below 20.15.6.1, below 20.18.4.1, below 26.1.2.1, and 26.2 itself. The KEV entry directs federal agencies to apply mitigations under BOD 26-04 on a deadline three days after the catalog addition, and records ransomware campaign use as unknown.

The Zimbra flaw is the reminder that "exploited" and "trivially exploitable" are different claims [[s16]]. CVE-2026-73570 is KEV-listed at 8.9 High — not Critical — a CWE-78 OS command injection that requires the optional zimbra-snmp package to be installed and SNMP notifications enabled, and is fixed in versions from 10.1.20. An unauthenticated attacker sending specially crafted requests can execute operating-system commands as the Zimbra user, and the supplied reporting says exploitation began before public disclosure and can occur via crafted email without user interaction; the CVSS vector's high attack complexity and changed scope reflect that this is not a one-size-fits-all mail-server takeover. **Analysis:** the practical question for defenders is whether the SNMP component is present, since servers that do not match that prerequisite do not satisfy the described conditions.

Apple's CVE-2026-86950 is an out-of-bounds write now KEV-listed at 8.8 High, with a first public proof-of-concept in circulation [[s36]]. The trigger is a PDF carrying a crafted embedded font that crashes unpatched iPhones and Macs; the released code produces a crash rather than code execution, and the excerpt cuts off before resolving whether that crash can be turned into a working exploit. Apple has said the issue may have been used in an extremely sophisticated attack against specific targeted individuals on iOS before version 27, and fixes ship in iOS and iPadOS 26.7.1, macOS Sequoia 15.8.1 and macOS Tahoe 26.7.1. The delivery path hinted at in the headline is a hint, not a supplied finding. **Analysis:** a crash-only PoC with a user-interaction prerequisite keeps near-term risk targeted rather than mass, but it raises the incentive to weaponise a bug that is confirmed as exploited.

## Breaches

The Pentagon's Defense Manpower Data Center is notifying millions of service members that hackers stole their data following a breach of the department's human resources management system; the headline puts the figure above three million people [[s32]]. No CVE, root cause or actor is supplied, so the significance here is scale and confirmation rather than mechanism.

Bitget has confirmed that attackers stole $387.5 million, attributing the intrusion to a zero-day in third-party security products on the basis of investigation findings it cites from SlowMist, and says a customised attacker tool was recovered [[s37]]. No CVE identifier or named actor appears in the supplied text, and the excerpt is truncated mid-account. **Analysis:** if a third-party security product really was the entry point, this is exchange supply-chain risk again — but that reading rests on an investigation summary we only see in part.

DIVD says its own network was breached through a chain of two zero-days in the open-source Zammad ticketing system [[s45]]. No CVE IDs are supplied for either flaw, and the "AI-driven" framing in the headline is not substantiated by the truncated excerpt. **Analysis:** two undisclosed flaws in a ticketing system used for vulnerability handling would be notable for anyone running similar infrastructure, but chain details, the AI claim and impact remain unverified on this evidence.

## Industry

Police took control of the KillSec ransomware operation's leak site, secured at least 110 terabytes of data stolen from victims, and identified an alleged 16-year-old administrator [[s9]]. **Analysis:** the seized victim data is the operation's real footprint; the age is an allegation, not an established fact, and the story supplies no detail on charges or further suspects.

## Research

More than 543,000 credentials exposed in public repositories were still valid at the time of analysis, despite the platform's measures to prevent accidental leaks of sensitive data [[s49]]. **Analysis:** validity is the part that matters — exposed strings are cheap, live secrets are the exposure — though the figure says nothing about which services were affected or whether credentials were counted more than once.

kev.vulnerabilityName: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager Hex Encoding Vulnerability
kev.shortDescription: Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager contains a hex encoding vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to access an affected system with privileges of the admin user due to improper handling of URI encoding in an HTTP request.
kev.requiredAction: Apply mitigations in accordance with vendor instructions, ensuring compliance with CISA’s BOD 26-04 Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk (see URL in Notes) guidance and CISA’s “Forensics Triage Requirements” (see URL in Notes). Follow applicable BOD 26-04 guidance for cloud services or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable. Stakeholders are responsible for evaluating each asset's internet exposure and ensuring adherence to BOD 26-04 patching guidelines.

nvd.description:
A vulnerability in the API session-based authentication management of Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to access an affected system with privileges of the admin user.

This vulnerability is due to improper handling of URI encoding in an HTTP request, which allows the request to bypass an authentication rule that is intended to restrict access to a specific API endpoint. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted HTTP request to the API of the affected system. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to bypass authentication and gain access to the API as the admin user.

selected.angle: CISA's KEV listing and an Oct 3 federal remediation deadline make this 9.8-rated Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager auth bypass the most urgent patch on the board today.

 shell commands by manipulating serialized class types in the OpenWire

instantiate any class on the classpath.

Users are recommended to upgrade
 both brokers and clients to version 5.15.16, 5.16.7, 5.17.6, or 5.18.3 
which fixes this issue.

A vulnerability in the API session-based authentication management of Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager could allow an unauthenticated, remote attacker to access an affected system with privileges of the admin user.

This vulnerability is due to improper handling of URI encoding in an HTTP request, which allows the request to bypass an authentication rule that is intended to restrict access to a specific API endpoint. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted HTTP request to the API of the affected system. A successful exploit could allow the attacker to bypass authentication and gain access to the API as the admin user.
